facts.raw_span: multiple painless nodules on the fingers of both hands
vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts
discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of his right arm and forearm
denied trauma or insect bites
his cow had similar lesions on its teats
3–4 firm, non-tender nodules with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema
mild tenderness and increased warmth along the medial right arm and forearm
Dermoscopy (10×) of one nodule showed an erythematous area with central ulceration and crust
yellow-white streaks, brown dots, a structureless whitish area partially surrounding the ulcer, an erythematous ring, and dot vessels

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms, including painless nodules and vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts, along with the presence of similar lesions on his cow, are consistent with Orf virus infection, a zoonotic disease.
The patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker and the presence of similar lesions on his cow suggest Paravaccinia virus infection, a zoonotic disease that can cause skin lesions.

The patient's symptoms, including painless nodules and vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts, along with the presence of similar lesions on his cow, are consistent with Cowpox virus infection, a zoonotic disease.
The patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker and the presence of similar lesions on his cow suggest Pseudocowpox virus infection, a zoonotic disease that can cause skin lesions.

rationales.F05: Similar lesions on the cow's teats suggest a zoonotic infection, with Orf virus being a strong candidate due to its common occurrence in sheep and goats, but also possible in cows.
rationales.F06: Firm, non-tender nodules with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema are typical of Orf virus and Paravaccinia virus infections.
rationales.F08: Dermoscopy findings of an erythematous area with central ulceration and crust are consistent with Orf virus and Paravaccinia virus infections.
rationales.F09: Dermoscopy findings of yellow-white streaks, brown dots, and dot vessels are characteristic of viral infections such as Orf virus and Paravaccinia virus.
